title: Category sort ignores capitals and puts numbers in counting order
custom_preconds:
Setup (manual QA tester and Claude session)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in as an Admin at {Location-A} (for example Staging Heavy Duty - 9919), with the Settings - Parts permission.
  • Category {Category-A} (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PC44 alpha) exists.
  • Category {Category-B} (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PC44 Beta) exists.
  • Category {Category-C} (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PC44 tier 9) exists.
  • Category {Category-D} (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PC44 Tier 10) exists.
  • Fixed rule part {Part-A} (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PC44-1) is at {Location-A} in category {Category-D} with fixed price (for example 15.00).
  • Fixed rule part {Part-B} (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PC44-2) is at {Location-A} in category {Category-C} with fixed price (for example 15.00).
  • Fixed rule part {Part-C} (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PC44-3) is at {Location-A} in category {Category-B} with fixed price (for example 15.00).
  • Fixed rule part {Part-D} (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PC44-4) is at {Location-A} in category {Category-A} with fixed price (for example 15.00).
  • You are on a page other than Pricing and the Pricing Search box is empty.
custom_steps:
1. Go to Settings and click Pricing in the Parts group of the Settings menu.
  2. Click the Fixed rules tab.
  3. Wait until the loading indicator on the Fixed rules tab disappears.
  4. Click the Category column header.
  5. Move the mouse pointer away from the column headers.
  6. Read the order of {Part-A}, {Part-B}, {Part-C} and {Part-D}.
  7. Click the Category column header again.
  8. Move the mouse pointer away from the column headers.
  9. Read the order of {Part-A}, {Part-B}, {Part-C} and {Part-D}.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 6: the Category arrow points up and the rows read {Part-D} ({Category-A}), {Part-C} ({Category-B}), {Part-B} ({Category-C}), {Part-A} ({Category-D}). With the examples the categories read alpha, Beta, tier 9, Tier 10: capitals make no difference and 9 comes before 10.
  • Step 9: the Category arrow points down and the rows read {Part-A}, {Part-B}, {Part-C}, {Part-D}.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-11258; story SV-10136 (Story 3, Fixed Rules, sortable columns; story text re-synced to the PRD on 13 Oct 2026); PRD "Settings Pricing And Categories Sorting (Price/Category)", Confluence 578781186, version 21 (14 Oct 2026), S3-R7 (with S3-R4, S3-R5 for the click directions), read 14 Oct 2026; design canvas board 1.4 (Fixed rules - before and after), 13 Oct copy, unchanged on 14 Oct. Source-verified 14 October 2026; not yet build-verified (no Price/Category QA build exists).

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S3-R7: “Category sorts alphabetically, ignores whether letters are upper case or lower case, and compares numbers inside a category name as numbers.”
  • S3-R4: “When the user clicks a sortable column header that is not currently sorted, the list sorts by that column: A to Z for Part number and Category, highest first for Fixed price (S3-R8).”
  • S3-R5: “When the user clicks that same header again, the list re-sorts in the opposite direction.”
